summary: Two plausible gaps do not survive source-level challenge. The completion weights come from one fixed global family of at most ten tails, and the split-pair contradiction explicitly handles member distinctness and equal coordinate projections. The newly clarified singleton-trace sentence agrees with the inherited proof. No repair is needed.

checks.scope: Possible illicit reuse of a key-dependent weight budget
checks.method: Challenge whether different keys might use different ten-unit budgets; read UniqueDesignTails.tail_projection_injective and ten_design_tails_card_le_ten, and compare with the fixed tails D and key_heavy definitions in ProfileAConcentrated.
checks.observation: W is fixed once the design pair is fixed. Projection to a B-design triple is injective: two distinct outsider extensions of the same tail, together with its x-star extension, are three distinct members with exactly that common tail. Center omission and support disjointness establish distinctness. Every relevant completion lies in this same W and has exactly one A-point, so total weight is |W|≤10 for all keys simultaneously. The heavy-pair argument does not reset its budget per key.

checks.scope: Possible missing distinctness or intersection hypothesis in split completions
checks.method: Read CompletionCompatibility.intersecting_link_edges_have_shared_block_trace, completion_tail_intersects, split_completions_card_le_four, and ProfileASplit.no_split_pair; reconstruct the equal-edge, singleton-overlap and disjoint cases.
checks.observation: Equal A-edges use their existing design block; singleton overlap uses a block through the common point avoiding both other endpoints. Its star member is distinct from both completions because it contains x, while they omit x. If both coordinate pairs are disjoint, the two completions and their disjoint anchor already form an empty-core sunflower. The formal caller supplies intersecting completions by this anchor argument, and equal completions are separately handled when projecting. Thus the four-completion bound has no hidden distinctness or intersection assumption.
